title: Frequently Asked Questions
body:
**Where is the festival?**
Telluride Town Park, at the east end of Telluride's main street. If you are standing downtown, walk east on Colorado Avenue until the buildings stop and the park starts. It is about ten minutes on foot from one end of town to the other, so nothing here is far.

**What time do gates open?**
Gates open at 11:00 AM Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. Music on the Main Stage starts at noon and runs to 10:30 PM each night. Late-night club shows start around 10:00 PM at venues in town and in Mountain Village.

**Can I bring a chair or a blanket?**
Yes. Low-back chairs only, and there is a designated blanket area in front of the Main Stage. Please do not set up a chair in the blanket zone or a tall chair anywhere near the front — the field slopes very little and everyone behind you will notice.

**Can I leave and come back?**
Yes, re-entry is allowed all three days with your wristband on. Do not take it off. A cut or stretched wristband is a void wristband, and the Box Office cannot replace one.

**Is there an ATM?**
Two, one just inside the Main Gate and one on Food Row. Most vendors take cards, but the lines are shorter when you have cash.

**What about the weather?**
September in the San Juans means warm afternoons, cold nights, and a real chance of an afternoon thunderstorm. See the Altitude & Hydration page — it is the single most useful thing in this app.

**Is the festival family friendly?**
Very. Kids ten and under get in free with a ticketed adult, and the Kids' Tent runs a singalong and an instrument petting zoo most mornings. There is a beer garden for the 21+ pours, and it is fenced.

**Something is different than what this says.**
This app updates itself. If a set time moves or the gates change, it will show up here within a few minutes without an app update. When in doubt, the Info Booth by the Main Gate is staffed all day.

title: Gondola & Shuttles
body:
**The gondola is free, and it is the best way to move around.**
The gondola connects the town of Telluride to Mountain Village over the ridge. It is genuinely free — no ticket, no pass, no tap. The ride is about thirteen minutes each way with a transfer at San Sophia Station at the top, and the view on the way over is one of the reasons people come here.

**Stations**
- **Station Telluride** — corner of San Juan Ave and Oak Street, on the west side of town. About a fifteen-minute walk from Town Park.
- **San Sophia** — the ridge-top transfer station. Get out and switch cabins here.
- **Station Village** — Mountain Village core, next to the conference center and most of the lodging.

**Hours during the festival**
Standard service runs roughly 7:00 AM to midnight. On festival nights the gondola runs later so people can get back from the late-night club shows — check the announcements in this app for the current last-car time, because it does change.

**Bikes, dogs, and gear**
There are dedicated cabins for bikes and dogs. Look for the sign at each station and wait for the marked cabin rather than putting a wet dog in with strangers.

**Galloping Goose town shuttle**
The Galloping Goose is a free loop bus through town, roughly every twenty minutes during the day. It is useful if you are staying at the west end and do not want the walk back after a long day at the park. There is a stop just outside the Town Park entrance.

**Driving and parking**
Do not plan on parking near Town Park. Telluride is a box canyon with one road in and out, and festival parking in town fills before noon. The realistic options are the free lots and garages in Mountain Village plus the gondola, or the Carhenge lot at the west end of town and a fifteen-minute walk. Rideshare and taxi service exists but is thin at 11:00 PM on a Saturday.

title: Park Rules & What to Bring
body:
**Bring**
- An empty reusable water bottle. Free refill stations are all over the park.
- Layers. A warm afternoon becomes a cold night quickly at this elevation.
- A rain shell. Not an umbrella — see below.
- Sunscreen and a hat. There is very little shade in the middle of the field.
- A low-back chair or a blanket.
- Cash for the vendors with the shortest lines.

**Leave at home**
- Umbrellas. They block sightlines and they are a bad idea when there is lightning.
- Glass containers of any kind.
- Outside alcohol. There is plenty inside.
- Pets. Service animals only inside the park during the festival. This is strictly enforced, and a hot dusty field is a miserable place for a dog regardless.
- Drones. The canyon is a controlled airspace and the answer is always no.
- Professional camera rigs with detachable lenses over about six inches, video cameras, and audio recorders, unless you are credentialed.
- Tents, canopies, and anything else that shades you at the expense of the fifty people behind you.

**On site**
- Wristbands stay on all weekend. Cut it and you have bought a new ticket.
- Re-entry is fine, all three days.
- The blanket area in front of the Main Stage is for blankets. Chairs go behind the line.
- Smoking and vaping are not permitted in the seating areas.
- Pack out what you can. Telluride runs an aggressive composting and recycling program and volunteers will help you sort at the stations.

**Beer garden**
The 21+ pours are inside a fenced beer garden. You need a wristband, and you get it by showing ID once at the entrance. Bring the ID even if you have not been carded in fifteen years.

title: Altitude & Hydration
body:
**Telluride sits at about 8,750 feet.** Town Park, where you will spend three days standing in the sun, is at roughly that elevation, and Mountain Village is higher still. If you flew in from sea level yesterday, your body has not caught up yet and it will let you know.

**What altitude actually feels like**
Headache, shortness of breath on a walk that should be easy, trouble sleeping the first night, a lower tolerance for alcohol, and a general sense of being slightly hungover without having earned it. This is normal for the first day or two. It is not normal to be confused, unsteady on your feet, or short of breath while sitting still — that is a medical tent visit, and the tents are staffed with oxygen whenever gates are open.

**What actually helps**
- **Drink more water than you think you need.** Twice as much. There are free refill stations across the park and no reason not to.
- **Go easy on the first day's beer.** A beer at 8,750 feet does not hit like a beer at sea level. Alternate with water; the Brewers Showcase pours are small on purpose.
- **Eat.** Altitude suppresses appetite right when you need calories.
- **Sleep low if you can.** If you have the choice between staying in town and staying higher, the first night in town is easier.
- **Take it slow the first day.** The hike up Bear Creek will still be there Sunday.
- **Skip the hangover heroics.** Ibuprofen for the headache, water, and time.

**Sun**
The UV at this elevation is roughly forty percent stronger than at sea level, and a September afternoon in a treeless field is a long time. Sunscreen in the morning and again after lunch, a hat, and sunglasses. People who ignore this spend Sunday under a canopy.

**Afternoon thunderstorms**
The monsoon pattern can hang on into September, and storms build over the peaks in the early afternoon and move through fast. If the festival calls a weather hold, it is because there is lightning within a few miles — leave the field, get away from the tall metal, and wait it out. The app will push an announcement and the Main Stage will tell you where to go. Holds usually last thirty to sixty minutes and the show almost always goes on.

title: Lodging & Camping
body:
**Book early.** Festival weekend is one of the busiest weekends of the year in Telluride and the town is small. If you are reading this in September and have not booked, look at Mountain Village, Ridgway, and Montrose before you look at town.

**In town**
Walking distance to Town Park, the highest prices, and the shortest walk home at midnight. Hotels, condos, and vacation rentals all book out months ahead.

**Mountain Village**
Up the gondola, ten to twenty minutes door to door, and usually cheaper than town for the same square footage. The gondola runs late on festival nights specifically so this works. Parking is free in the village garages, which matters more than people expect.

**Town Park Campground**
The festival campground is inside the park, which means you walk about ninety seconds from your tent to the Main Stage. It sells out fast and it is only available with a three-day pass. Quiet hours run 1:00 AM to 7:00 AM, and they are enforced by your neighbors more than by staff. Bring a warm bag — overnight lows in September can drop into the thirties.

**Other camping**
There is dispersed National Forest camping up Last Dollar Road, Ilium Valley, and Alta Lakes, plus commercial campgrounds down valley. Most of these are unimproved, some require a high-clearance vehicle, and none of them are a short drive at 1:00 AM. If you go this route, know your road before dark.

**Down valley**
Ridgway is about forty-five minutes, Montrose about ninety. Both have chain hotels at a fraction of the price. The tradeoff is the drive back over the pass after a long day, so plan a designated driver.

**Current listings and the official lodging partner are on tellurideblues.com.**

title: Tickets
body:
**Ticket types**
- **Three-day pass** — all three days, the best value, and the only ticket that makes you eligible for the Town Park Campground.
- **Single-day tickets** — Friday, Saturday, or Sunday. Released in limited blocks and usually the last thing to go.
- **VIP** — reserved viewing area, dedicated bar and restrooms, shade, and a separate entrance.
- **Kids ten and under** get in free with a ticketed adult.
- **Late-night club shows** are ticketed separately from the festival and sell out independently. A festival pass does not get you in.
- **Brewers Showcase** tasting sessions are included with festival admission for guests 21 and over.

**Wristbands**
Your ticket becomes a wristband at the gate or at will call. Put it on correctly the first time — it must be snug, and it stays on all weekend. Cut, stretched, or transferred wristbands are void, and the Box Office cannot issue a replacement.

**Will call**
Box Office on the west side of Town Park, 10:00 AM to 8:00 PM. Bring photo ID matching the purchaser's name and your confirmation, on your phone is fine.

**Buying and reselling**
Buy from the festival's official channels only. Every year people show up with a screenshot of a ticket somebody sold them twice, and there is nothing the Box Office can do about it. If a deal seems too good, it is.

**Refunds**
Tickets are non-refundable. The festival happens rain, shine, or hail — weather holds are part of the deal, not a cancellation.

**Buy at tellurideblues.com/tickets.**

title: Accessibility
body:
**Start at the Info Booth.** It is just inside the Main Gate and it is where accessibility check-in happens. Staff there can issue an ADA wristband, point you to the viewing platform, and answer anything this page does not cover.

**Getting into the park**
The Main Gate is the accessible entrance. The path from East Colorado Avenue to the gate is paved. Inside, Town Park is a grass field — mostly flat, but it is grass, and it gets soft after rain. A wheelchair with wider tires does noticeably better than a narrow indoor chair.

**Viewing**
There is an ADA viewing platform with a sightline to the Main Stage, with room for a guest alongside each patron. It is first come, first served, and it fills for headline sets. There is also a designated accessible seating area near the Blues Stage.

**Restrooms**
Accessible stalls are at the east end of the Food Row restroom bank and at the Main Stage bank. They are marked on the map in this app.

**Parking and drop-off**
There is a small accessible parking area and a drop-off point near the Main Gate. Space is genuinely limited; the gondola from Mountain Village is fully accessible and is often the easier option. Both gondola stations have level boarding, and staff will slow or stop a cabin on request.

**Service animals**
Service animals are welcome. Pets are not permitted in the park during the festival. Bring water for your animal; the field is hot and dusty by afternoon.

**Hearing and sight**
ASL interpretation can be arranged for Main Stage sets with advance notice — contact the festival before the event rather than at the gate. If you would find a quiet space useful, ask at the Info Booth; there is a low-stimulation area away from the stages.

**Medical**
Two medical tents, one near the Main Stage and one on the west side, staffed whenever gates are open, with oxygen available. If you use a medication that needs refrigeration, the Info Booth can help.

**Tell us what we missed.** This page is maintained by festival staff and gets better every year because people write in.
